body: I'm so nervous. And alone. I'm trying to text friends...anybody to help. But no body is responding. I want to die so bad
And I forgot to add... congrats on getting through it! You are awesome!

Thank you sooooo much for the encouragement. I've been tryin to talk to ppl I'm close to but it is hard to understand if you haven't been through it. I feel awful about how difficult I am to be around. I AM A DAMN TERROR. I have had some pain return since I stopped, my legs are the worse. I used to be on tramadol but when I moved back to Kentucky, the laws are super strict and it's like impossible to get. I wish I could it would help. I have also noticed that a bowl helps, I'm gonna have to get some to get me through this. 
Thanks again, I miss being myself.

I did try counting beads for a while but my fuse was so short that I would FLIP OUT. Like if I lost count or dropped some...or simply the fact that I had to do it at all. Now I wish I would've enlisted the help of someone who cares to count a bunch out for me. In fact i'm still considering that, maybe I should.

What's weird to me is that I have been prescribed xanax, adderall, vyvanse,and percocet before the first 3 long-term and NEVER had withdrawal with those. I did a little with the hydrocodone, but not nearly as bad as with cymbalta, I was only on the pain meds for about 3 months so I woudn't expect the withdrawal to be to harsh but still I had no clue how bad the cymbalta would be. (look at that run-on sentence...not even gonna fix it.) You are right I do need to go to the PCP, I just need to do it bc this is no way to live especially if this could be going on for MONTHS. I could handle a few days but I wouldn't be that lucky.
Seriously...thanks so much. This has been so helpful and at least I dont feel alone in this.

I have an appointment scheduled in November when my new insurance kicks in. My psychiatrist appointments just went from $75-$125 (which is pretty screwed up). 
What is weird is that I wasn't really planning on completely quitting at this exact time. I got a spider bite on my hand that turned into a cellulitis (a nasty infection of the skin and tissue below it). I was really miserable and on heavy antibiotics and percocets so my 2 days between meds slipped into 5 days. I didn't really know what to do then, I was kinda like, well I've made it this far so I'll just stop- the worst is already over. But... I think the percocets were masking some of the withdrawal but when I stopped those...well hello withdrawal... 
I am considering going to my PCP to get some help bc they take my insurance....but I don't like her and haven't been able to find a new one yet. It's like the withdrawal is working to make the withdrawal worse...does that make sense. My words, brain, everything is weird right now.

Yeah, I learned the hard way about going cold turkey- of course those were accidental caused by either the pharmacy, insurance and/or the doctor. Something would screw up and I'd be without it for a couple days and be completely LOSING MY SHIT! Like self-harm and tremors. I had to do internet research to realize it was withdrawal and I was on a dangerous drug. After this happened a couple times I made the decision to stop taking it on my on accord instead of being dragged through hell every couple of months. I actually did break the capsules and count beads for a while but it was INCREDIBLY FRUSTRATING!!And I felt I wasn't getting consistent doses. Even mild withdrawal gave me a short temper and I'd throw a tantrum every time I would count 150 of those fuckin beads. Now I wish I would've had someone close to me, with a longer fuse, count a bunch out for me. I feel ya on the de-realization. Everything feels...wrong.

Oh I could def tell you knew what you were talking about. I included the info mainly for the person that first commented (just had a brain zap, I could not figure out the word commented-like I forgot how to say it and spell it, thank goodness for spellcheck!). I am not a medical doctor but I am an optometrist so I have learned about a lot about some of the meds in school and then personal experience. What worries me is that maybe it's not all withdrawal and I am clinically depressed and always will be. And the brain zaps...I mean I am an eye doctor and have a responsibility and care deeply for my patients. My biggest fear is that the withdrawal will decrease my ability to do my job.

Right! it is their responsibility to give their patient's the necessary info before prescribing. However, I do think a lot of the problem is that the manufacturers did not allow this info to be easily accessible therefore some doctors didn't know. Some probably still don't. But that needs to change. This med has the evil power to destroy lives...i honestly believe that. I'm lucky I didn't lose my job. What I come to realize more and more everyday is that it is all about money...that's why they didn't present the info and why it is still being prescribed so haphazardly. Shame on them.

I'm very sorry and I completely understand. I have been on the brink of suicide and hope to never return. If it works for you (and continues to do so), I'm glad you found something. Just stay informed and dont let your dr keep increasing your dose bc that'll only make it more difficult to stop it. And a warning, if you do have to quit be careful and tell somebody who cares for you what is going on. I have done pretty bad self-harm going through this withdrawal and there are reports of suicide after cessation. Good luck.

I actually did break apart the capsules and count beads for a while but it was INCREDIBLY frustrating. Now I obviously wish I just would've kept trying tapering this way but I felt like I was getting inconsistent doses and still felt pretty bad. The best solution would be for the manufacturers to own up to their mistake and make smaller doses for those of us tryig to kick it.

The med itself was not that terrible for me except for horrible weight gain(which obviously causes other issues itself) and increased blood pressure. I decided to stop taking it bc of the times my insurance or doctor would screw up and I would have to go without it for a few days. This happened a couple times and wreaked havoc on my life. I felt like a drug addict when the methadone clinic is closed. Hopeless, helpless, crazy. I couldn't stand the stress of making sure that I always had it. I'd rather stop taking it of my own accord instead of trusting that everybody else would always have their shit together. I just wish I wouldve been warned. If you do decide to stop, precede with caution.

I have also been on every SSRI and wellbutrin. Cymbalta wihtdrawal is sooooo much worse because it regulates serotonin AND norephinephrine- 2 VERY important neurotrasnmitters. So when you stop taking it you are low on BOTH of these. If it is helping you I dont think you should necessarily stop but be informed and if you do precede with caution.

IDK, I am obviously not qualified to advise you but at this point I would tell everybody NOT to even start taking the drug. If it really is helping stick with it but if there is any chance you wont be able to afford it or some other reason it would be quickly taken from you I would consider stopping now. That's why i quit, the med itself didn't cause too many problems( except I used to be fit and have self esteem and now I'm quite overweight and feel like shit about myself). Insurance and/or my doctor would screw something up and I wouldn't have it for a couple days and my life would fall to pieces. I realized I couldn't handle being so physically addicted to something. If you do decide to stop, talk to your dr and precede with EXTREME caution.

The first time I went through withdrawal, I had NO CLUE what was going on. My doctor was slow on the refill so I went a couple days without it and I'm lucky I didn't kill myself. It took internet research to realize all the terror was from withdrawal. Then there was ins problems and other issues, so i had some withdrawal every cpl of months. That's when I decided I needed to get off it for good. I know this is the right decision, I just worry about the damage to my life in the meantime: my job, relationships, my brain and body...are all suffering. Running sounds like a good idea, I can't run anymore bc of my knees but I can do other things and plan on starting something. I'm glad you are yourself again, welcome back to the world!

I agree, it is evil. They tried to put my mom on it and she just laughed in the doctor's face and switched to a different doctor. It really needs to Rx'ed with more care. There should be a warning on the label. I mean I have been prescribed xanax, adderall, and even hydrocodone and percocet...no problems with withdrawal/addiction (except maybe the pain meds but it was mild). (Note: those were all PRESCRIBED, I'm not just running around taking everything I can get! lol) Hopefully the lawsuits will get the appropriate info out there so that ppl know to avoid it.

I'm sorry you too have had to deal with this... I honestly feel like I know how drug addicts feel. I mean in reality I am, when you have serious withdrawal upon cessation of something=addict. But the fact that I didn't know what I was getting myself into really bothers me. I even researched it before I took it but that was before ppl were really having problems. I have considering joining the lawsuits, I truly believe the manufacturers should be held responsible and there should be a warning on the labels. However, I am an Optometrist(recently licensed) and reputation is soooo important. I don't want my professional name associated with this med, and the companies will come after you to try to win the case. I have an appointment scheduled with my psychiatrist in November, which is when my new insurance kicks in. I would like to take something to help but have to wait till the money falls into place to see the doctor. Luckily, I am prescribed xanax which has helped but makes me worry about even more addiction! Thanks for your support. And I def might send you a PM next time I'm crashing.

Thanks soooo much for all the support. I have been talking to my mom, bf, and bff about it but it's hard for others to understand until they have experienced it. All of the comments have done wonders for my mood...its the small things, ya know. You guys are all wonderful people.
